title: Certificates of Deposit: sizing a maximum in-term add-on as the smallest room
content:
## Scope

When the owner of a Certificates of Deposit certificate asks to move as much as the certificate will take into it as an in-term add-on, this rule states how the size of the add-on is taken from the rooms measured for it.

## Rule

1. Three rooms are measured on the certificate as it stands when the add-on is made.
2. The add-on accepted is the smallest of the three rooms, rounded half up to 2 decimal places.
3. The rooms are never added together, averaged or taken in turn: only the single smallest one sets the size.

## Worked witness (hypothetical rooms)

| Room | Hypothetical value |
|---|---|
| First room measured | 20000.00 |
| Second room measured | 5412.505 |
| Third room measured | 9800.00 |

- Smallest room: 5412.505.
- Rounded half up to 2 decimal places: 5412.51. That is the add-on accepted.
- Wrong readings: taking the largest room (20000.00) would exceed two of the limits; adding rooms together has no basis.

## Points of judgement

**Two rooms are equal and smaller than the third. Which one sets the size?**
Either: the size is the smallest value, whichever room it comes from.

**Is the size rounded down to stay safely inside the limits?**
No. It is rounded half up to 2 decimal places.
